Empagliflozin in adults with heart failure

In adults with heart failure, does empagliflozin compared with placebo reduce the first occurrence of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalisation for heart failure -- the outcome both trials register as their primary?

It proves the ARITHMETIC between the extraction table and the headline. It cannot detect a wrong count, a swapped arm or a mis-specified model, because it re-runs the same inputs.

Derived by ssot/absolute_effect.py for any topic with a pooled ratio measure AND a declared indirectness argument. Where either is missing it DECLINES with a reason rather than emitting a table the review has not licensed — a ratio becomes an absolute effect only against a baseline risk, and a baseline risk belongs to a population.

This topic holds a pooled HR of 0.7708 but says nothing about how far it transfers -- no rated indirectness domain and no declared question_pico. An absolute table built here would invite a reader to apply this estimate to their own population with no statement of whether that is supported, and arithmetic is not a substitute for that statement.

Inter-assessor agreement

This assessment is DUAL — two assessors from different model families, the second asked blind. The agreement rate is withheld pending adjudication. Both readers were given this review’s decision rule; an earlier version of this sentence said the blinding had withheld it, and that was wrong. What the 10 domain comparison(s) show is a reading difference that runs in OPPOSITE directions by domain — on domains 1 to 3 the second assessor more often declines to judge at all, and on domains 4 and 5 it more often judges low. A single agreement rate averages those two behaviours into one number that describes neither. Both assessors’ per-result judgements are shown in the table above, unadjudicated, and neither is this review’s finding. No adjudication has been performed, so this review holds no final risk-of-bias judgement for these results.

HR 0.7708 (0.7 to 0.8488), 95% interval

Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) | Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF). random-effects, estimator REML, k = 2.

τ² 0 · I² 0% · Q 0.2785 on not stated df

Favours: the intervention (direction of benefit not recorded for this outcome)

Q = 0.368949 on 1 df, I-squared 0.0 per cent, tau-squared 0.0 under REML: the two trials agree closely. That agreement is not the main uncertainty here. Both trials registered this endpoint as time to first event and this pool combines odds ratios computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that ran for different lengths of time. An odds ratio over unequal follow-up is not a hazard ratio and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. Direction and rough magnitude are not in doubt -- both favour empagliflozin, both intervals exclude no effect -- but read the pooled number as an approximation to the quantity the trials estimated, not as that quantity. Two trials agreeing about an odds ratio over unequal follow-up agree about something neither of them set out to measure.

The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason.

How to read this: How this pool combines the two trials is a weaker claim than what they measured. Both trials register the same primary endpoint, verified word for word -- the registered strings differ only by the word 'the'. But both register it as time to first event, and this pool combines odds ratios computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that did not run for the same length of time. An odds ratio over unequal follow-up is not a hazard ratio and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume they mean. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. The direction and rough magnitude here are not in doubt -- both trials favour empagliflozin and both intervals exclude no effect -- but the pooled number should be read as an approximation to the quantity the trials estimated, not as that quantity. Recorded 2026-08-20. Whether this pool is recomputed from the published hazard ratios is a decision that has been referred and not taken; the limitation is stated either way, because a reader must not be able to reach the estimate without meeting it.

Risk of bias, both assessors

⬇ SVG (vector) 8 KB

Only the vector format is offered for this figure, by choice: it is line art — discrete marks, glyphs and labels — which SVG reproduces exactly at any size, so a raster would add weight without adding fidelity. The build was able to rasterise; it was asked not to.

Every cell carries BOTH independent cross-family assessments and they are not reconciled: showing one column would be a reconciliation presented as an observation. Glyph as well as colour, so the panel survives greyscale printing and colour-blind reading. A trial with no judgement is shown as a row of not-assessed markers rather than omitted, so a gap in the assessment cannot be mistaken for a clean assessment. It rests on a risk-of-bias judgement that this review has not finalised: two assessors read every contributing result independently, they disagree, and no adjudication has been performed, so this review holds no final risk-of-bias judgement for these results. Cochrane rates certainty per outcome by aggregating the risk-of-bias judgements of the results contributing to it, so a certainty rating cannot be more final than the risk-of-bias assessment it reads. Both trials register the same primary endpoint, verified word for word -- the registered strings differ only by the word 'the'. An odds ratio over unequal follow-up is not a hazard ratio and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume they mean. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title

Empagliflozin in adults with heart failure1

A claim on this object is withdrawn as false. It asserted that no published synthesis pools this review's two trials. Emperor-pooled is exactly that: a prospectively planned pooled analysis of EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved, at individual-patient level, with multiple indexed publications. It is not an obscure record and it is not a near-match; it is a pooled analysis of precisely the two trials, designed as one before either reported. The claim is withdrawn and not deleted. What it said, that it was false, and what is true are all recorded here, because a claim that quietly disappears cannot be audited and a reader who acted on it has no way to learn that it was wrong. What this means for the comparison: the published-synthesis comparison on this object was drawn against a stated absence that does not exist. It should be re-run against EMPEROR-Pooled. That is work, not a correction, and it is not done here.2

Abstract

Question. In adults with heart failure, does empagliflozin compared with placebo reduce the first occurrence of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalisation for heart failure -- the outcome both trials register as their primary?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects model with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials), 22 August 2019 version as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook; and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) | Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF): hazard ratio 0.771 (0.7 to 0.849) across 2 trials; and no statistical heterogeneity was detected (I-squared 0%), though heterogeneity cannot be reliably assessed with two trials.3

Results

The pooled hazard ratio for multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) | Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) was 0.771 (0.7 to 0.849) across 2 trials, against placebo.1

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.278. Q = 0.368949 on 1 df, I-squared 0.0 per cent, tau-squared 0.0 under REML: the two trials agree closely. That agreement is not the main uncertainty here. Both trials registered this endpoint as time to first event and this pool combines odds ratios computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that ran for different lengths of time. An odds ratio over unequal follow-up is not a hazard ratio and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. Direction and rough magnitude are not in doubt -- both favour empagliflozin, both intervals exclude no effect -- but read the pooled number as an approximation to the quantity the trials estimated, not as that quantity. Two trials agreeing about an odds ratio over unequal follow-up agree about something neither of them set out to measure.2

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.3

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is stored verbatim on this review object at `results.by_outcome.<outcome>.r_output.verbatim`. It is not reproduced as an Extended data section in this article; an earlier version of this sentence said it was, and no such section exists.4

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 at the level of each reported result, by two assessors reading independently. Their judgements differ on 2 of the 2 results and no adjudication has been performed, so this review holds no final risk-of-bias judgement for these results. Assessor 1 recorded: 2 at some concerns. Assessor 2 recorded: 2 at no information. Both are shown in the risk-of-bias table; neither is the review's finding. The per-domain judgements behind them are recorded with the extracted data.1

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

This certainty rating is pending, not rated. It rests on a risk-of-bias judgement that this review has not finalised: two assessors read every contributing result independently, they disagree, and no adjudication has been performed, so this review holds no final risk-of-bias judgement for these results. Cochrane rates certainty per outcome by aggregating the risk-of-bias judgements of the results contributing to it, so a certainty rating cannot be more final than the risk-of-bias assessment it reads. The rating this object currently records, and the steps behind it, are shown below as the work so far rather than as this review's answer. No level is published for this outcome -- not the recorded one, not a more cautious one, and not a midpoint -- because choosing one would be the judgement that has not been made.3

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/empagliflozin-hf-auto-full-review/appraisal/the screen of published syntheses.json. 130 records matched, 25 retrieved, 5 appraised, 125 not read. No included-study table was read for any of the five: their trial sets are inferred from abstract text, participant totals and search cut-off dates, and every check resting on an inferred set says so.1

Limitations

What this review does not give a clinician: any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.1

1 of 12 considerations informed; 11 not addressed. The empty cells are the point. An evidence-to-decision framework needs values, resource use, equity, acceptability and feasibility; the Handbook places those with the review authors and a guideline panel, and they are not derivable from trial data. A panel handed a complete map of what is unanswered is better served than one handed prose that reads as though it covered all twelve. Every informed row names the field it is informed by.

Page standard

UNSTAMPED — unknown-version. This page carries no build_stamp, so the standard it was built to cannot be established. That is a statement about the record, not a claim that the page is below standard.

Every number on this page is projected from a single canonical object, and each measured cell names the source analysis it was read from. That is what is machine-checked. It does not establish that the underlying sources are right, only that this page faithfully reports them.

What is being estimated

primaryHRtime to event2

The registry records an analysis of time to event for 2 of the contributing trials.

The pooled quantity and the trials' recorded analysis are of the same kind.

Both intervals, and which one this page reports

OutcomekPooledRandom-effects WaldModified Hartung–KnappWider by
primary20.7710.700 to 0.8490.413 to 1.4406.48×

At two trials this page reports neither interval as the answer, and says why. With k = 2 the modified interval uses t on ONE degree of freedom — a multiplier of 12.71 against 1.96 — because two trials carry almost no information about how much results vary between trials. The resulting interval is wide by construction and would be nearly as wide whatever the trials had found, so it should not be read as evidence that the treatment does not work: that width is the degrees of freedom, not the data. The Wald interval has the opposite fault — it treats a between-trial variance estimated from two numbers as if it were known, and is too narrow for the same reason. Both are printed above so a reader can see the size of the gap rather than inherit whichever one an author preferred.

The modification is the floor at q* = 1. Unmodified, Hartung–Knapp can return a narrower interval than Wald whenever Q < k−1 — which would let the estimator that carries more uncertainty appear more confident. Flooring it means extra care can never buy a tighter answer.

For primary: 2 trials, τ² = 0.0000, q* = 1.00 (at the floor — without it the more careful estimator would have returned a narrower interval than the Wald one). The t multiplier on 1 degrees of freedom is 12.71 against 1.96 for the normal, so the modified interval is 6.48× wider on the analysis scale.

What has changed since these trials were last synthesised

No comparator is designated for this question, so this page does not state how current it is relative to one. Which published review answers the same question is a judgement, and this component refuses to make it by taking whichever identifier appears first — doing exactly that produced a search date from an adherence review of observational studies on an earlier run. The object mentions PMIDs 32865377; none is marked as the comparator.

What the pooled effect means in people

primary — not converted. The pooled quantity is HR, and a hazard ratio is a ratio of rates over person-time; converting it needs a baseline RATE and a stated horizon, and this object holds neither. It is refused rather than approximated.

Safety, and every other outcome these trials reported

This object records no outcome besides the one pooled above. That is a statement about what has been extracted into this review, not about what the trials measured: a trial that reported harms this review has not extracted will look, from this page, exactly like a trial that reported none.

Which counts were used, and what difference it makes

This object records event counts from one source per trial and no alternative was sought, so this page cannot tell you whether the registry and the publication agree. ⚠️ That is not the same as saying they do. A registry posts counts as submitted and a publication reports them after endpoint adjudication; where those differ, the adjudicated figure is the trial's own final answer, and a review that never compared them cannot say which it is using.

What quantity this is, and what the trials actually analysed

This object does not record what quantity the contributing trials analysed, so this page cannot say whether the quantity it pools is theirs. ⚠️ That is an unchecked assumption, not a clean bill: a risk ratio over binary counts and a hazard ratio over person-time are different quantities, and a review that pools the first while the trials analysed the second will differ from them whenever follow-up differs between arms.

What a clinician or a programme should take from this

  • On primary, the pooled estimate is 0.771 (0.700 to 0.849) and the interval excludes no difference.

Each statement above is emitted only when a specific condition holds in this review's own object; none is written by hand. This section makes no recommendation: what to offer, to whom, at what cost and against what alternative is a judgement this page does not hold the inputs for.

What this page cannot tell a clinician, and why. magnitude — no absolute effect for primary (refused: the measure is HR, not a risk ratio). where it holds — no stratum reads as demonstrated. where it has not been shown — no stratum reads as not demonstrated. harms — no harm outcome is held at the trial-report tier. what it is not — no outcome is recorded as absent or not measurable. what it is conditional on — the object records no background care delivered alongside the intervention, so this page cannot say what its estimate is on top of. efficacy versus use — the object records no adherence finding.

How certain this is, and why — the certainty profile

GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.

primary — k = 2

No rating is shown. the object does not record a starting certainty, so the certainty cannot be derived from its own steps and a stored value would be an assertion rather than a result.

DomainReadingLevelsReason
risk of biasno downgrade—BOTH results are SOME_CONCERNS, and the driver is the same in each: D2, deviations from intended intervention, is NO_INFORMATION because neither NEJM methods section is in PMC open access -- 32865377 and 34449189 both checked, neither returns a PMC record. D1, D3, D4 and D5 are LOW on sources read and named. RATED DOWN BECAUSE UNASSESSED IS NOT LOW, and the reason is recorded as OUR ACCESS rather than an observed flaw in the trials -- P49, with the attempted route on the object.
inconsistencyno downgrade—I-squared is 0.0% with tau-squared 0 over k=2. Handbook 10.10.2: I-squared describes the PROPORTION of variability beyond chance, not the amount, and at k=2 it is estimated with almost no information -- so this is 'no inconsistency DETECTED' rather than 'consistency established'. Not rated down, and the limit of that statement is on the record.
indirectnessno downgrade—THE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE WITH NO RECORDED ESTIMAND PROBLEM. Both trials register the SAME primary, word for word -- 'Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure' -- each registers ONE primary rather than a set to choose from, and the pooled quantity is that registered quantity. Population, intervention, comparator and outcome all match the question asked. NOT SERIOUS IS A FINDING HERE, not a default: it is the contrast with the other two topics that makes it worth stating.
imprecisionno downgrade—The published interval 0.6825 to 0.8409 excludes the null. BUT THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL DOES NOT: with Hartung-Knapp on t at k-1 = 1 degree of freedom the same point estimate carries 0.385 to 1.4907, and that interval CROSSES ONE. At k=2 the between-trial variance is estimated from a single degree of freedom, so the narrow interval is a property of the estimator rather than of the evidence. Handbook 15.6.2 on optimal information size. THE POINT ESTIMATE IS UNCHANGED; what differs is the precision claim, which is why nothing downstream catches it.
publication biasno downgrade—NOT ASSESSED RATHER THAN ASSESSED AS ABSENT. Funnel-plot asymmetry and its tests are uninformative below about ten studies -- Handbook 13.3.5.4 -- and these pools carry two or three. 'Undetected' here means NOBODY LOOKED WITH AN INSTRUMENT THAT COULD SEE, not that publication bias is unlikely. Not rated down, because rating down on an unmeasurable domain would invent a defect.

Certainty LOW. The risk-of-bias domain reads the per-result RoB 2 assessments made 2026-08-20 and named above, not a topic-level summary; indirectness reads the estimand findings recorded on this pool.

6 classes we know about and cannot yet detect

Named because a taxonomy that lists only what it catches is marketing.

  • narrative-contradicts-its-own-table — prose that disagrees with the table beside it -- semantic, no instrument exists
  • value-does-not-reconcile-with-its-source — a stored number that does not follow from the document it cites; needs the source in hand, and we hold the primary report for a minority of trials
  • planned-field-shown-as-observed — a registered plan displayed in a field labelled as observation -- found by hand on this page's follow-up figure
  • prior-synthesis-value-presented-as-primary — a competitor's extraction reported as our own read; labelled here by hand, not detected
  • subgroup-claim-beyond-the-trial-strata — a subgroup statement the trial's own strata do not support
  • adjudicated-versus-submitted-counts — registry and publication disagreeing on event counts; detectable only where both are held
